summary: Completed Microsoft SSO integration testing. All 9 backend tests passed (100%). Frontend tests verified: Microsoft SSO button visible on LUMI login page, clicking it redirects to login.microsoftonline.com with correct tenant/client IDs, and LumiMessenger correctly handles #session_id in URL hash for SSO callbacks.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py: Microsoft SSO properly configured - /microsoft/config returns configured:true when AZURE_CLIENT_ID and AZURE_TENANT_ID are set
auth.py: /microsoft/login correctly builds OAuth authorization URL with all required params (client_id, response_type, redirect_uri, scope)
auth.py: /microsoft/callback properly exchanges auth code for tokens via Microsoft Graph API, creates user and session
auth.py: /session/validate is a generic endpoint that works for both Google and Microsoft SSO session tokens
LumiLogin.jsx: handleMicrosoftLogin at line 41 correctly calls POST /api/auth/microsoft/login and redirects to auth_url
LumiMessenger.jsx: SSO callback handler at line 89 properly extracts session_id from URL hash and tries both Google and generic session validation
context_for_next_testing_agent: Microsoft SSO fully configured and working. Backend: /api/auth/microsoft/config (GET), /api/auth/microsoft/login (POST returns auth_url), /api/auth/microsoft/callback (GET handles OAuth callback), /api/auth/session/validate (POST validates any session token). Frontend: 'Sign in with Microsoft' button on LumiLogin.jsx redirects to Microsoft login, callback redirects to /lumi#session_id=TOKEN which LumiMessenger handles via session/validate endpoint. Note: Full OAuth callback flow cannot be automated (requires real Microsoft user interaction).
